conditions.exact_rule_quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952
conditions.description: The relied-on subletting, assignment, or other parting-with-possession conduct must occur on or after the statutory cutoff date.
conditions.scope: Applies to each section 14(1)(b) transfer alternative.

conditions.description: The tenant sub-let or assigned the whole or any part of the premises.
conditions.scope: Subletting or assignment branch of section 14(1)(b).

conditions.exact_rule_quote: otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises
conditions.description: The tenant otherwise parted with possession of the whole or any part of the premises.
conditions.scope: Parting-with-possession branch of section 14(1)(b); the target court's later interpretation is not imported into this input-side rule definition.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord
conditions.description: The relevant transfer conduct occurred without the landlord's written consent.
conditions.scope: Applies to any section 14(1)(b) transfer alternative.

bindings.stage: eviction petition before Additional Rent Controller
bindings.reason: The landlord alleged transfer conduct after 9 June 1962, which would fall after the statutory 9 June 1952 cutoff if the allegation were accepted; this remains a claim, not an established fact.

bindings.stage: documentary evidence later recounted on Supreme Court appeal
bindings.reason: The reported business sale on 1 January 1970 supplies a post-cutoff time anchor, while the inventory expressly leaves unresolved whether the sale transferred possession of the premises.

bindings.stage: eviction petition before Additional Rent Controller
bindings.reason: The landlord expressly alleged subletting or assignment to Baldev Raj and Sat Pal; the binding preserves that allegation only as a candidate evidentiary proposition.

bindings.stage: eviction petition before Additional Rent Controller
bindings.reason: The landlord expressly alleged that Jagan Nath otherwise parted with possession to his sons; this is retained as a claim rather than treated as true.
The tenant side claimed Jagan Nath remained in exclusive possession and continued his business, which, if accepted, weighs against the proposition that he parted with possession.

The landlord testified that the sons operated the business in partnership and were in possession of the premises, supporting a candidate inference of parting while not resolving exclusivity or legal control.
The landlord denied that Jagan Nath remained in possession and asserted that he had retired, supporting the candidate proposition of divestment while preserving the claim status.

bindings.stage: documentary evidence later recounted on Supreme Court appeal
bindings.reason: The reported sale of the business to the sons can support a candidate transfer-of-control inference, but the inventory expressly marks as unknown whether it transferred possession of the premises.

bindings.stage: documentary evidence later recounted on Supreme Court appeal
bindings.reason: The sons' reported partnership under the same business name in the same premises supports their use or occupation, while the inventory leaves the extent of their possession or control unresolved.

bindings.stage: Supreme Court appeal review of documentary record
bindings.reason: Sat Pal's reported electricity application as sole proprietor is a candidate indicator of business control, but the inventory expressly leaves its effect on possession or tenancy rights unknown.
The Additional Rent Controller found unlawful parting with possession. This preserves the lower-court procedural finding as an input candidate and does not treat it as target-court adoption.

bindings.stage: eviction petition before Additional Rent Controller
bindings.reason: The landlord alleged that the asserted transfer conduct occurred without written consent; the input-side binding preserves this only as a claim.

element_targets.reason: The target merits discussion does not expressly decide the statutory cutoff-date element. Post-cutoff dates appear in the record, but the target court resolved the ground on the transfer alternatives and written-consent question, so the temporal condition is not inferred from the disposition.

target_refs.quote: There is also no evidence that there has been any subletting or assignment.

element_targets.reason: The target court expressly stated that there was no evidence of subletting or assignment; this is treated as failure of proof rather than a declaration that every underlying factual allegation was false.

target_refs.quote: it cannot be said that the father had divested himself of the legal right to be in possession.
it cannot be said that the tenant had parted with possession.

element_targets.reason: Applying its legal-possession analysis, the target court expressly rejected parting with possession because Jagan Nath had not divested himself of the legal right to possession.

target_refs.quote: There is no dispute that there was no consent in writing of the landlord in this case.

element_targets.reason: The target court expressly accepted the absence of written landlord consent as undisputed.

target_refs.quote: There is also no evidence that there has been any subletting or assignment.
it cannot be said that the tenant had parted with possession.
The eviction order is accordingly set aside.

issue_target.reason: The fixed section 14(1)(b) ground is not supported at the target stage: absence of written consent was accepted, but the target court found no evidentiary basis for subletting or assignment and expressly rejected parting with possession, then set aside the eviction order.
